- **Hallucination / unpredictability vs strict SLAs** — the lead Q&A concern; mitigation = guardrails + determinism, but structurally a hard problem at scale.
- **Pricing-model uncertainty** — direction is toward **outcome-/per-transaction/per-success pricing**, but "we don't really see that play out as much today... very early." (Tempers the outcome-based-pricing optimism around NEWSPULSE from Q4FY26.)
- **Per-job deflation risk** — content-production cost deflation *could* pressure per-job pricing; management leans on **Jevons' paradox** (more automation → more total work) as the offset. Watch whether volume expansion actually outruns per-unit price erosion.
- **Tech immaturity** — VLMs today are "very expensive and very slow"; world models / custom audio-video models still "early phase."
- **Hyperscaler / horizontal-SaaS encroachment** — addressed via the vertical-context moat argument, but a standing structural risk.

bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **"Metadata explosion" named as the industry's single largest bottleneck** (with a supporting Amagi report) — the clearest articulation yet of Amagi's structural wedge.
- **$1 tech : $2–$4 human toil** — a crisp sizing of the agentic-automation opportunity in media prep.
- Customers adopt AI **expansionarily, not to cut cost** ("more channels, more revenue") — corroborates the 126% net-retention / upsell narrative from Q4FY26.
- **Outcome-based pricing "not playing out today"** — a mild caution against over-crediting NEWSPULSE-style outcome pricing near-term.
- The real tech frontier is **world models + hundreds of custom audio-video models / VLMs, NOT LLMs** ("it's not a Claude or GPT or Gemini that solves video/audio") — differentiates Amagi's "eyes-and-ears" approach from generic GenAI hype and explains the GPU (not token) cost base.
- **Agentic Discovery** (consumer-owned conversational interface displacing OTT destinations) is flagged as the next disruption to the *distribution* layer Amagi's customers depend on — an optionality *and* a risk to watch.

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Cyber security and platform reliability — Customers rely on Amagi's technology for critical broadcast and streaming operations where continuous uptime is vital. A security breach, technology failure, external provider interruption or friction during customer upgrades could disrupt services and expose the Company to financial, regulatory or reputational consequences.
- Dependence on third-party cloud infrastructure and its pricing — Technology costs — primarily cloud infrastructure — are 70.1% of other expenses and rise with platform activity. Managing third-party cloud infrastructure requires navigating price shifts and temporary cost overlaps during major migrations, so direct-cost control is not fully in the Company's hands.
- Strategic execution and AI innovation risk — Growth depends on picking the right product priorities and shipping at market pace. Delays in product development, changing customer requirements or slower adoption could curb customer expansion; introducing AI capabilities into live broadcast systems requires exhaustive testing, which can lengthen sales cycles.
- Acquisition identification and integration risk — Strategic acquisitions are an explicit catalyst for market entry and capability expansion, and the Company has earmarked IPO proceeds for inorganic growth. Realising the full value of M&A requires disciplined target identification and seamless operational integration.
- Leadership readiness and talent density — Execution depends on strong leadership, high talent density and adequate succession for critical roles. Gaps in leadership experience, limited bench strength or delays in developing future leaders could affect decision-making and business continuity, in a market for specialised engineering skills that remains highly competitive.
- Revenue assurance and commercial governance — Reliance on manual processes and offline workflows across the customer lifecycle creates operational friction. Differences between contractual terms, complex service fulfilment and multi-party delivery models could cause administrative delays, reconciliation challenges or potential revenue leakage.
- Market dynamics with customer and geographic concentration — The media industry is changing rapidly as audiences shift platforms and advertising models evolve. Exposure to certain large customers and to North America increases sensitivity to changes in customer spending and market conditions — a structural concentration risk.
- Operational governance and multi-jurisdiction regulatory compliance — Running the platform across many countries requires staying aligned with local laws and ahead of evolving privacy rules such as GDPR, CCPA and India's DPDPA as the Company expands across regions.

outlook.body:
CEO framed AI transformation across the **four stages of the media value chain** (analogised to a retail/FMCG supply chain: factory → warehouse → logistics → store):

- **1. Production (content creation).** GenAI (he named Google "Omni"/Veo, "Nano Banana," Runway) is starting to deflate the cost of content production; "AI-first studios" fusing AI tooling with human storytelling are emerging globally. View: **cost of content production will deflate**, forcing the economics of every downstream stage to be rethought. Caveat — "live sports might be the only non-AI content to survive" ("gladiator sports").
- **2. Preparation (metadata / packaging) — Amagi's core.** The "**metadata explosion**": thousands of hours of content × 40+ countries × multi-language subtitles/dubbing/artwork/ratings/compliance = today a huge human-labour "chore." He cited their own recently-published report flagging **metadata as one of the industry's largest bottlenecks.** **Agentic infrastructure** ("glorified coffee machines" — software that predicts/anticipates/acts) replaces this chore work. Illustration: a TV scheduler's task that "takes 8 hours" done overnight by an agent, letting one person run "tens of channels."
- **3. Distribution / transaction — "inter-company agent transactions."** Content creators ↔ platforms across 40+ countries currently transact via manual email/phone negotiation. Future = **agent-to-agent** commercial/legal/technical negotiation and a marketplace layer ("time compression... orders of magnitude" faster legal agreements).
- **4. Discovery — "Agentic Discovery."** Consumers shift from OTT-destination browsing to a **personal conversational bot** (ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini-type) that owns the interface and surfaces content across all platforms based on mood/history — a long-dated disruption to the distribution layer.
- **Content transformation optionality (not just automation):** removing the human+hardware bottleneck lets a *single* live match be rendered as **many personalised stories** (tactical fan vs home fan vs Gen-Z multi-cam/chat views); and legacy libraries repurposed into new formats (e.g. a 3.5-hr *Sholay* condensed into 3-minute micro-dramas / 30-min intense episodes). Microdrama flagged as an active growth area.

outlook.body:
- Maximise customer lifetime value through platform depth, product expansion and geographic reach, continuing to invest in cloud infrastructure, AI capabilities and go-to-market capacity
- Land-and-expand: grow primarily by expansion within existing customers who add products, channels, destinations and geographies on largely recurring or usage-linked pricing
- Convert usage expansion into structural operating leverage on a largely shared technology and operating base, then translate earnings into free cash flow
- Advance from cloud infrastructure into 'Intelligence' — embedding domain-specific AI and reasoning-based autonomous agents across production, preparation, distribution, monetization and consumption, moving the industry from software automation to autonomous operations
- Use Cloud Modernization as the entry point into the broader platform ecosystem, funnelling customers onward into Streaming Unification and then Monetization and Marketplace
- Broaden market reach through partnerships and localisation — e.g. the ADAMS partnership in Latin America and localisation across more than 100 languages

- Simplify commercial structures, automate service-to-billing workflows and strengthen revenue-assurance controls to support a more scalable operating model
- Build leadership from within via the A100 flagship leadership programme and strengthen succession planning for critical roles
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Amagi is an asset-light, cloud-native software business with no manufacturing footprint; expansion is platform build-out, geographic reach and inorganic additions rather than plant capacity. The AR describes capital expenditure of ₹22 crore on new offices and infrastructure during FY26 (against ₹4 crore in FY25), with depreciation and amortisation remaining low at 1.4% of revenue, and management states that capital expenditure requirements are relatively low so operating cash flow should largely flow through to free cash flow. Growth investment is directed at cloud infrastructure, AI capabilities and go-to-market capacity: of the fresh-issue IPO proceeds, ₹5,500.64 million is earmarked for technology and cloud infrastructure and ₹2,223.87 million to fund inorganic growth and general corporate purposes; against net proceeds received of ₹7,724.51 million, ₹740.57 million had been utilised as at the year under review with no deviation reported by the monitoring agency. Footprint expansion during the year came through the group structure rather than capacity: Amagi AI Private Limited was incorporated in India (21 March 2025) and funded with ₹7,00,000 of equity share capital on 25 April 2025 to build AI-led media solutions, while voluntary liquidation of the step-down subsidiary Argoid Analytics Private Limited was initiated in November 2025. Reach expanded to 9,425 channel deliveries across 40+ countries, 407 distributors and localisation across more than 100 languages, supported by partnerships such as ADAMS in Latin America. Capital-allocation intent for the post-IPO liquidity of ₹1,664 crore is to invest first in organic growth, product capabilities and infrastructure, followed by selective acquisitions that strengthen technology, capabilities or market access. No capacity-expansion project, commissioning date or ramp timeline is disclosed.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Media infrastructure moving to the cloud: the global Media and Entertainment industry is projected to reach $3.6 trillion by CY2029 with technology spending expected to reach $68 billion, and since much of the industry still relies on legacy infrastructure this creates a meaningful long-term opportunity
- Roughly 90 percent of broadcast operations still rely on legacy on-premises infrastructure, spending four dollars on manual labour for every dollar spent on software — the gap Amagi is positioned to bridge
- Growth of CTV, FAST and digital advertising: global CTV advertising spend reached $42.5 billion, growing at more than 10% annually and capturing a quarter of total TV ad spend, increasing demand for distribution, ad-insertion and yield technology
- The market for AI across media and streaming operations is expected to expand from 5 billion dollars towards 20 billion dollars by 2029
- AI-led agentic automation reduces manual effort across metadata generation, content scheduling, monitoring and ad placement, letting media companies handle more content and complexity
- Durable revenue growth driven by expansion within existing customers — NRR of 125.9% in FY26, USD 1 million+ customers up from 28 to 35, and 29 net new customers added
- Structural operating leverage: operating expenses declined to 58.7% of revenue and Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 10.3%; incremental revenue can be supported on a largely shared technology and operating base
- Management expects a growing share of earnings to convert into cash because capital expenditure requirements are relatively low, so operating cash flow should largely flow through to free cash flow, subject to working capital and taxes
- Direct costs (technology and delivery) rise with platform activity — channels, destinations and impressions supported — and remained stable at approximately 31% of revenue
- Share-based compensation is declining as a share of revenue (12.4% of revenue in FY24 to 7.0% in FY26) as earlier grants vest, improving conversion of Adjusted EBITDA into profit after tax; the expense is primarily non-cash
- Industry shifts are increasing the number of workflows, channels and destinations media companies must manage, creating more opportunities for customers to use Amagi across their operations
- Post-IPO liquidity of ₹1,664 crore in cash and investments with no debt provides financial flexibility to fund the next chapter in AI and autonomous operations

risks.note: Customers rely on Amagi's technology for critical broadcast and streaming operations where continuous uptime is vital. A security breach, technology failure, external provider interruption or friction during customer upgrades could disrupt services and expose the Company to financial, regulatory or reputational consequences.

Technology costs — primarily cloud infrastructure — are 70.1% of other expenses and rise with platform activity. Managing third-party cloud infrastructure requires navigating price shifts and temporary cost overlaps during major migrations, so direct-cost control is not fully in the Company's hands.
risks.risk: Dependence on third-party cloud infrastructure and its pricing

risks.note: Growth depends on picking the right product priorities and shipping at market pace. Delays in product development, changing customer requirements or slower adoption could curb customer expansion; introducing AI capabilities into live broadcast systems requires exhaustive testing, which can lengthen sales cycles.
risks.risk: Strategic execution and AI innovation risk

risks.note: Strategic acquisitions are an explicit catalyst for market entry and capability expansion, and the Company has earmarked IPO proceeds for inorganic growth. Realising the full value of M&A requires disciplined target identification and seamless operational integration.

Execution depends on strong leadership, high talent density and adequate succession for critical roles. Gaps in leadership experience, limited bench strength or delays in developing future leaders could affect decision-making and business continuity, in a market for specialised engineering skills that remains highly competitive.

Reliance on manual processes and offline workflows across the customer lifecycle creates operational friction. Differences between contractual terms, complex service fulfilment and multi-party delivery models could cause administrative delays, reconciliation challenges or potential revenue leakage.

The media industry is changing rapidly as audiences shift platforms and advertising models evolve. Exposure to certain large customers and to North America increases sensitivity to changes in customer spending and market conditions — a structural concentration risk.
risks.risk: Market dynamics with customer and geographic concentration

risks.note: Running the platform across many countries requires staying aligned with local laws and ahead of evolving privacy rules such as GDPR, CCPA and India's DPDPA as the Company expands across regions.

one-line thesis: No numbers to score — this is a thematic session, not a quarter update. The signal value is the CEO's detailed framing of how AI restructures the **entire media value chain** — production → preparation → distribution/transaction → discovery — and his repeated positioning of the labour-heavy "metadata explosion" and agentic automation as *the* opportunity (i.e. exactly Amagi's wedge). Read it as strategic backdrop that reinforces the FY26 thesis (AI-led operating leverage + market expansion for content creators), not as fresh operating data.

growth verticals / optionality (the subs:
CEO framed AI transformation across the **four stages of the media value chain** (analogised to a retail/FMCG supply chain: factory → warehouse → logistics → store):

- **1. Production (content creation).** GenAI (he named Google "Omni"/Veo, "Nano Banana," Runway) is starting to deflate the cost of content production; "AI-first studios" fusing AI tooling with human storytelling are emerging globally. View: **cost of content production will deflate**, forcing the economics of every downstream stage to be rethought. Caveat — "live sports might be the only non-AI content to survive" ("gladiator sports").
- **2. Preparation (metadata / packaging) — Amagi's core.** The "**metadata explosion**": thousands of hours of content × 40+ countries × multi-language subtitles/dubbing/artwork/ratings/compliance = today a huge human-labour "chore." He cited their own recently-published report flagging **metadata as one of the industry's largest bottlenecks.** **Agentic infrastructure** ("glorified coffee machines" — software that predicts/anticipates/acts) replaces this chore work. Illustration: a TV scheduler's task that "takes 8 hours" done overnight by an agent, letting one person run "tens of channels."
- **3. Distribution / transaction — "inter-company agent transactions."** Content creators ↔ platforms across 40+ countries currently transact via manual email/phone negotiation. Future = **agent-to-agent** commercial/legal/technical negotiation and a marketplace layer ("time compression... orders of magnitude" faster legal agreements).
- **4. Discovery — "Agentic Discovery."** Consumers shift from OTT-destination browsing to a **personal conversational bot** (ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini-type) that owns the interface and surfaces content across all platforms based on mood/history — a long-dated disruption to the distribution layer.
- **Content transformation optionality (not just automation):** removing the human+hardware bottleneck lets a *single* live match be rendered as **many personalised stories** (tactical fan vs home fan vs Gen-Z multi-cam/chat views); and legacy libraries repurposed into new formats (e.g. a 3.5-hr *Sholay* condensed into 3-minute micro-dramas / 30-min intense episodes). Microdrama flagged as an active growth area.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Context as the moat** (his central competitive claim): for a **vertical**, mission-critical media platform, "the reasoning might become commoditized, but the **context** of the enterprise... becomes the most important moat." Whoever owns the *business + technology + operating context* drives future workflows — his answer to whether hyperscalers/horizontal SaaS threaten a vertical player.
- **Production-grade reliability as a barrier:** on strict SLAs (he referenced ~"99.9999%"), "demos and POCs are the easiest; the hardest is to get them to production" — bringing **determinism/guardrails to an indeterministic (hallucination-prone) problem** at content-factory scale is the engineering moat.
- (Both stated at the industry / "vantage-point-of-a-vertical" level — he declined to make them Amagi-specific — but they map directly onto Amagi's positioning.)
margins & cost dynamics: Framed for *customers*, not Amagi: today **"for every $1 spent on technology there is $2–$4 of human toil"** — the automation TAM. AI here is mainly **human-cost reduction**; cost is **GPU/custom-model** cost (not "token" cost — "token cost is a very small part... video is custom models/GPU"), and "the cost of GPU is nowhere comparable to the human cost" being displaced. Net effect he expects is **expansionary, not cost-cutting** — most customers use AI to add channels/reach/new revenue, not to shrink spend.
risks & watch-items:
- **Hallucination / unpredictability vs strict SLAs** — the lead Q&A concern; mitigation = guardrails + determinism, but structurally a hard problem at scale.
- **Pricing-model uncertainty** — direction is toward **outcome-/per-transaction/per-success pricing**, but "we don't really see that play out as much today... very early." (Tempers the outcome-based-pricing optimism around NEWSPULSE from Q4FY26.)
- **Per-job deflation risk** — content-production cost deflation *could* pressure per-job pricing; management leans on **Jevons' paradox** (more automation → more total work) as the offset. Watch whether volume expansion actually outruns per-unit price erosion.
- **Tech immaturity** — VLMs today are "very expensive and very slow"; world models / custom audio-video models still "early phase."
- **Hyperscaler / horizontal-SaaS encroachment** — addressed via the vertical-context moat argument, but a standing structural risk.
management quality / tone: Confident, evangelical ("once in a lifetime transformation," "biggest change," "truly excited") but **disciplined and compliance-aware** — Amoolya and Baskar repeatedly and firmly refused company-specific questions, keeping strictly to the stated educational scope. Thoughtful, first-principles framing (retail/FMCG analogies, coffee-machine agent metaphor, Jevons' paradox). Signals a deliberate new **investor-education cadence** (periodic thematic webinars, feedback-driven).
non-obvious takeaways:
- **"Metadata explosion" named as the industry's single largest bottleneck** (with a supporting Amagi report) — the clearest articulation yet of Amagi's structural wedge.
- **$1 tech : $2–$4 human toil** — a crisp sizing of the agentic-automation opportunity in media prep.
- Customers adopt AI **expansionarily, not to cut cost** ("more channels, more revenue") — corroborates the 126% net-retention / upsell narrative from Q4FY26.
- **Outcome-based pricing "not playing out today"** — a mild caution against over-crediting NEWSPULSE-style outcome pricing near-term.
- The real tech frontier is **world models + hundreds of custom audio-video models / VLMs, NOT LLMs** ("it's not a Claude or GPT or Gemini that solves video/audio") — differentiates Amagi's "eyes-and-ears" approach from generic GenAI hype and explains the GPU (not token) cost base.
- **Agentic Discovery** (consumer-owned conversational interface displacing OTT destinations) is flagged as the next disruption to the *distribution* layer Amagi's customers depend on — an optionality *and* a risk to watch.

demand_drivers.body:

- The market for AI across media and streaming operations is expected to expand from 5 billion dollars towards 20 billion dollars by 2029

- Durable revenue growth driven by expansion within existing customers — NRR of 125.9% in FY26, USD 1 million+ customers up from 28 to 35, and 29 net new customers added
- Structural operating leverage: operating expenses declined to 58.7% of revenue and Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 10.3%; incremental revenue can be supported on a largely shared technology and operating base
- Management expects a growing share of earnings to convert into cash because capital expenditure requirements are relatively low, so operating cash flow should largely flow through to free cash flow, subject to working capital and taxes
- Direct costs (technology and delivery) rise with platform activity — channels, destinations and impressions supported — and remained stable at approximately 31% of revenue
- Share-based compensation is declining as a share of revenue (12.4% of revenue in FY24 to 7.0% in FY26) as earlier grants vest, improving conversion of Adjusted EBITDA into profit after tax; the expense is primarily non-cash
- Industry shifts are increasing the number of workflows, channels and destinations media companies must manage, creating more opportunities for customers to use Amagi across their operations
- Post-IPO liquidity of ₹1,664 crore in cash and investments with no debt provides financial flexibility to fund the next chapter in AI and autonomous operations

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Framed for *customers*, not Amagi: today **"for every $1 spent on technology there is $2–$4 of human toil"** — the automation TAM. AI here is mainly **human-cost reduction**; cost is **GPU/custom-model** cost (not "token" cost — "token cost is a very small part... video is custom models/GPU"), and "the cost of GPU is nowhere comparable to the human cost" being displaced. Net effect he expects is **expansionary, not cost-cutting** — most customers use AI to add channels/reach/new revenue, not to shrink spend.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Amagi is an asset-light, cloud-native software business with no manufacturing footprint; expansion is platform build-out, geographic reach and inorganic additions rather than plant capacity. The AR describes capital expenditure of ₹22 crore on new offices and infrastructure during FY26 (against ₹4 crore in FY25), with depreciation and amortisation remaining low at 1.4% of revenue, and management states that capital expenditure requirements are relatively low so operating cash flow should largely flow through to free cash flow. Growth investment is directed at cloud infrastructure, AI capabilities and go-to-market capacity: of the fresh-issue IPO proceeds, ₹5,500.64 million is earmarked for technology and cloud infrastructure and ₹2,223.87 million to fund inorganic growth and general corporate purposes; against net proceeds received of ₹7,724.51 million, ₹740.57 million had been utilised as at the year under review with no deviation reported by the monitoring agency. Footprint expansion during the year came through the group structure rather than capacity: Amagi AI Private Limited was incorporated in India (21 March 2025) and funded with ₹7,00,000 of equity share capital on 25 April 2025 to build AI-led media solutions, while voluntary liquidation of the step-down subsidiary Argoid Analytics Private Limited was initiated in November 2025. Reach expanded to 9,425 channel deliveries across 40+ countries, 407 distributors and localisation across more than 100 languages, supported by partnerships such as ADAMS in Latin America. Capital-allocation intent for the post-IPO liquidity of ₹1,664 crore is to invest first in organic growth, product capabilities and infrastructure, followed by selective acquisitions that strengthen technology, capabilities or market access. No capacity-expansion project, commissioning date or ramp timeline is disclosed.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Asset-light, cloud-native platform built from inception — depreciation remained low at 1.4% of revenue and capital expenditure requirements are described as relatively low
- High switching costs from embedding into mission-critical live broadcast workflows; customers enter through a single channel, event or regional workflow and progressively migrate more of their estate onto the stack
- Land-and-expand economics: Net Revenue Retention of 125.9% in FY26 and customers generating more than USD 1 million rising from 28 to 35
- Proprietary operational data moat — 17 years of operational history, over 42.4 billion annual ad impressions and telemetry from more than 9,000 active channel deliveries train Amagi Intelligence on signals competitors cannot replicate
- Ecosystem flywheel: more content attracts broader distribution reach, which lifts impression volumes and monetisation yields, which draws more premium content onto the platform
- Demonstrated structural operating leverage — over three years S&M and customer-success expense fell from 44.0% to 24.0% of revenue and R&D from 33.0% to 23.1%
- Proven reliability at scale on the world's most-watched live events, including Super Bowl LX, the Oscars, the Winter Olympics, the Grammys, UEFA football and the FIFA women's world cup
- Distribution breadth — 407 distributors and localisation capability across more than 100 languages
- Debt-free balance sheet with cash and investments of ₹1,664 crore as at March 31, 2026, following IPO primary proceeds

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Hallucination / unpredictability vs strict SLAs** — the lead Q&A concern; mitigation = guardrails + determinism, but structurally a hard problem at scale.
- **Pricing-model uncertainty** — direction is toward **outcome-/per-transaction/per-success pricing**, but "we don't really see that play out as much today... very early." (Tempers the outcome-based-pricing optimism around NEWSPULSE from Q4FY26.)
- **Per-job deflation risk** — content-production cost deflation *could* pressure per-job pricing; management leans on **Jevons' paradox** (more automation → more total work) as the offset. Watch whether volume expansion actually outruns per-unit price erosion.
- **Tech immaturity** — VLMs today are "very expensive and very slow"; world models / custom audio-video models still "early phase."
- **Hyperscaler / horizontal-SaaS encroachment** — addressed via the vertical-context moat argument, but a standing structural risk.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **"Metadata explosion" named as the industry's single largest bottleneck** (with a supporting Amagi report) — the clearest articulation yet of Amagi's structural wedge.
- **$1 tech : $2–$4 human toil** — a crisp sizing of the agentic-automation opportunity in media prep.
- Customers adopt AI **expansionarily, not to cut cost** ("more channels, more revenue") — corroborates the 126% net-retention / upsell narrative from Q4FY26.
- **Outcome-based pricing "not playing out today"** — a mild caution against over-crediting NEWSPULSE-style outcome pricing near-term.
- The real tech frontier is **world models + hundreds of custom audio-video models / VLMs, NOT LLMs** ("it's not a Claude or GPT or Gemini that solves video/audio") — differentiates Amagi's "eyes-and-ears" approach from generic GenAI hype and explains the GPU (not token) cost base.
- **Agentic Discovery** (consumer-owned conversational interface displacing OTT destinations) is flagged as the next disruption to the *distribution* layer Amagi's customers depend on — an optionality *and* a risk to watch.
